summary: Morondava Airport (MOQ/FMMV) is a regional airport serving the coastal city of Morondava on Madagascar's western coast, functioning as the primary air gateway to the Menabe region. It is best known as the access point for the iconic Avenue of the Baobabs, one of Madagascar's most photographed natural landmarks. The airport handles domestic flights, connecting this remote area to the capital Antananarivo.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Morondava Airport?
A: Domestic carriers, primarily Tsaradia (the domestic subsidiary of Air Madagascar), operate scheduled flights connecting Morondava with Antananarivo.

Q: How far is Morondava Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers from central Morondava, making it a short drive to most hotels and guesthouses in town.

Q: Is Morondava Airport used for international flights?
A: No, the airport primarily handles domestic flights, with no scheduled international service. International travelers typically connect through Antananarivo's Ivato International Airport.

Q: What is the best time to fly to Morondava?
A: The dry season from April to November is recommended, as it offers clearer skies and better road conditions for visiting the Avenue of the Baobabs and surrounding attractions.
transport_tips: Taxis and hotel-arranged transfers are the most common ways to reach the airport from Morondava town, typically taking just a few minutes. Travelers heading to the Avenue of the Baobabs can arrange a taxi or private 4x4 directly from the airport, as the site lies about 20 km northeast of the city. It is advisable to confirm return transport in advance, as vehicles may be limited during peak tourist season.
local_tip: Schedule an early morning or late afternoon arrival or departure if visiting the Avenue of the Baobabs on the same day — the famous golden-hour light on the ancient baobabs is best experienced at sunrise or sunset, and the airport's proximity to the site makes this easily doable.
